parts.title: A Silent Square
parts.text: In the invented kingdom of Karvonia, a single **edict** from the ruler could close a school, ban a newspaper or send a neighbor into exile. The country was an **autocracy**, and no one had ever voted on anything. Alexei, a printer's apprentice, knew that the ruler wished to **subjugate** every town that questioned him. His master, a **dissident** who had once spent a year in jail for his opinions, kept a hidden press in the cellar.

parts.title: The Secret Pamphlet
parts.text: One midnight, Camila, a teacher, slipped into the cellar carrying pages of a **manifesto**. It demanded fair elections, open schools and an end to secret arrests. She was a **fervent** believer in reform, and her eyes shone as she read. The palace would call the pamphlet **sedition**, because it urged citizens to resist the crown, and anyone found with a copy might be punished. Alexei set the type anyway.

parts.title: The Square Fills
parts.text: Within months, the quiet discontent became open **rebellion**. In the hills, **insurgent** bands blocked roads and seized grain stores. A few army officers whispered about a **coup**, a sudden seizure of power, but Camila refused to join them. “Power taken by force only teaches the next ruler to rule by force,” she said. Idris, a young farmer, thought her plan too cautious, and his own ideas were far more **radical**: he wanted every title and privilege erased at once. Yet even he agreed that the old ruler must be removed, and thousands marched peacefully to **dethrone** him.

parts.title: What Came After
parts.text: In time, the ruler agreed to hold elections, and Alexei printed the very first ballots. The new government was imperfect, and reformers argued bitterly about how fast to change. Alexei learned that winning a revolution is easier than building a fair country. Justice, he decided, is not one victory but a habit that every generation must practice.

definitions.meaning1: A person who openly opposes the government's policies, especially where doing so is dangerous. Example: The dissident was arrested for criticizing the ruler in print.
definitions.meaning2: Openly disagreeing with official policy. Example: Dissident members of the club voted against the new rules.
definitions.studentChallenge: Police arrested the ___ for speaking out against the ruler's policies.

definitions.meaning1: An open, organized resistance to a ruler or authority. Example: The unfair salt tax sparked a rebellion in the northern provinces.
definitions.meaning2: A refusal to obey rules or follow expectations. Example: Wearing mismatched socks was her small rebellion against the dress code.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ began when townspeople refused to pay the unfair tax.

definitions.meaning1: A person who fights against an established government or authority. Example: The insurgents controlled the hills outside the capital.
definitions.meaning2: Rising up in revolt against authority. Example: The insurgent forces took over the radio station.
definitions.studentChallenge: The army searched the mountains for the armed ___ hiding there.

definitions.meaning1: A system of government in which one person holds unlimited power. Example: In an autocracy, the ruler's word is law.
definitions.studentChallenge: Citizens of the ___ had no way to vote the ruler out.

definitions.meaning1: Speech or action that encourages people to rebel against their government. Example: The old law punished sedition with a long prison sentence.
definitions.studentChallenge: The king accused the pamphlet's author of ___.

definitions.meaning1: A sudden takeover of a government by force, usually by the military or a small group. Example: A group of generals planned a coup to take over the government.
definitions.meaning2: A brilliant, unexpected achievement. Example: Landing the famous scientist as a speaker was a real coup for our small school.
definitions.studentChallenge: Officers seized the palace in a surprise ___ at dawn.

definitions.meaning1: A public statement of a group's beliefs, goals and plans. Example: The new party published a manifesto promising cleaner rivers.
definitions.studentChallenge: The club wrote a ___ explaining what it hoped to change.

definitions.meaning1: To bring under control by force; to conquer and dominate. Example: The empire tried to subjugate its neighbors one by one.
definitions.studentChallenge: The invading army hoped to ___ the whole region within a year.

definitions.meaning1: An official order given by a ruler or authority. Example: By royal edict, no one could leave the city after dark.
definitions.studentChallenge: The queen's ___ ordered all markets closed on holy days.

definitions.meaning1: To remove a ruler from power. Example: The rebels hoped to dethrone the cruel king.
definitions.meaning2: To defeat a champion or remove someone from a top position. Example: The young swimmer hoped to dethrone the reigning champion.
definitions.studentChallenge: The upstart team hoped to ___ last year's champions.

definitions.meaning1: Showing very strong, sincere feeling or enthusiasm. Example: She made a fervent promise to return home.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ fans cheered for hours after the victory.

definitions.meaning1: Extreme; calling for sweeping change. Example: The radical plan would rebuild the entire school system.
definitions.meaning2: A person who favors extreme change. Example: Once called a radical, she is now praised for her foresight.
definitions.studentChallenge: The mayor proposed a ___ change: closing downtown to all cars.
